comment_b6bceed0ee48.body: Can we actually say the sandbox should do a lookup? So this change just hands the sandbox a figaro identity and says do what you will. We aren’t doing oidc provider authenticated service calls for containers yet, we’re relying on people running the containers to deploy that. I think we already do this through env vars for local disk, so we just need to ensure it’s applied to the header if we send the bytes over a http connection or whatever, so that on spain and other nodes can manage sandboxed permissions congruently with figaros. On ingress, the figaro daemon trusts the caller. To distribute acorss nodes, you want some form of workload identity, and run the cli binary in the daemon. Cli client should pass along the name, but the identity should be authorized by a gateway on the nodes that are running figaros and authenticated there and then pass into the figaro for authorization, where they should be blocked if the are trying to talk to a figaro who has some permission that the other does have.

comment_f7efbd4b4e82.body: My thinking is for a "bring your own sandbox" design, but for a sandbox interface to be declared. I think there are multiple issues here. One is a role as a call identity.  I think we can expect to be wrapped by callers that provide a reliable figaro identity.  But we need to manage the lifecycle of the container in that case.  I'm thinking it would be convenient to allow an environment constructor to be injected as a dependency into the figaro fork runtime.  I think this would take theform ideally of lower level primitives.  One is one that we have mentioned before in plans, the "derived form".  Basically a libretto that can apply a transformation or action when another form changes .  that introduces the possibility of loops and cycles at runtime and we could probably quell that.  But it might be helpful to have this internally.  It would really just need to be a hook that passes a sequence number and which can write to a form as an output or perform some stateful action.  And we can ideally register a module in figaro that listens for this hook on a privleged system property, and listens in particular for updates to the sandbox address, and can be injected by a dependent caller to automatically provision a new sandbox address the a selected set of permissions, and then also apply those permission to the figaro.  So really it just needs to be a runtime hook on a figaro at creation time.  Not even one when forms change, just the ability to inject a runtime hook on mint.  Or actually, even better,  none of this, the sandboxes should just accept a header that has the figaro's name on it and know to automatically create a sandbox with those permissions or look one up by id if it doesnt exist, and the sandbox can sync its permission set by polling the ebac form if it wishes to.  That should be our response.  So final conclusion, we should ensure that all calls into a sandbox are sent with some marker that provides the figaro id, and encourage sandbox providers to use this id to lookup the permissionset of that figaro, which should have its permissions encoded in it's privileged system property, I think.  That information can be cloned, and by default we can have a pattern where we fork on patch and automatically apply a hierarchical narrowing of the permissionset.  Really protection levels, but more robust.  can you elaborate on that, answer on the issues, close the issues out that are obsolete with official guidance, draft a plan, and give it to me for review on keel?
